هو أنا ينفع أعلم أطفالي التسامح و أنا لما بيغلطوا مش بسامحهم ؟؟
أكيد لأ
لو أطفالي لما بيغلطوا بقولهم "مش هتكلم معاك، مش هسامحك دلوقتي ، إدخل الأوضة و متطلعش منها..."
*كدة أنا بوصلهم إني زعلان من شخصهم مش من الموقف
*و إن حبي ليهم مشروط بتصرفاتهم "أنا هحبك لما تعمل اللي أنا عايزاه، أنا هحبك لو معملش حاجة غلط..."
* وكمان بقولهم أنا بحبكم وقت لما أنا أعوذ مش وقت لما إنتم تعتذروا

إبتدي بنفسك و واري أولادك يعني إيه تسامح في معملتك معاهم و أكيد هما هيتزرع جواهم اللي إتربوا عليه

✨ The key to your baby’s sleep schedule? It’s all about knowing their cues! Understanding the difference between sleepy, tired, and overtired can make all the difference:

💤 Sleepy: Just the right time to settle down for a nap or bedtime. Look for subtle yawns, calm movements, or zoning out.

😴 Tired: They’re ready for sleep but may need some help winding down. You’ll see more rubbing of the eyes or fussiness.

😩 Overtired: They’ve passed their sweet spot. Cue meltdowns, difficulty falling asleep, and needing extra soothing.

Mastering these cues = smoother sleep transitions for both you and your baby! 🍼💤

Changing a diaper? “Now I’m taking off your diaper... let’s wipe clean!”
Bath time? “Here comes the warm water... splash splash!”

I’m going to continue to say this until people start listening….. 

Your anger is NOT a discipline tool!

When you yell in anger it is incredibly intimidating to your children…

 You think by shouting blue-murder it will show the kids how serious you are and how wrong their actions were….

The problem is children’s brains don’t absorb the  lesson you think you’re teaching ….

Instead it goes into survival mode. 

Their stress hormones spike, their heart races, and they focus on escaping the perceived threat: YOU. 

Instead of learning to listen, they learn to fear. Instead of feeling safe, they feel the need to escape and hide.

This isn’t the relationship you want.
And guess what… it isn’t what they want either 

So, what’s the alternative? 

➡️ Connection.

❌Connection doesn’t mean permissiveness. 

✅It means addressing behavior with firmness that is kind, rooted in respect and understanding. 

✅A connected child is more likely to listen, trust, and cooperate, not out of fear, but out of love.

👉Choose Connection Over Control every time!!!!!!

Instead of reacting with anger, stop yourself and CHOOSE to lean into connection. Ask yourself:

❓What is my child trying to communicate through their behavior?

❓What is driving their behaviour?

❓What do I need, to stay calm and in control of my own emotions so I can effectively parent right now?… because at the end of the day, where YOU lead is exactly where your children will follow.

I think the internet when used wisely, is awesome and gives us many awesome opportunities that we didn’t have maybe 10, 20 years ago…

Although I look back at my own parenting journey as a mother and see so many things I wish I knew 20 years ago that would have been helpful, at the same time I look back and in a lot of ways I’m glad social media wasn’t a thing when I was a young mum…

I think today we have reached a point where we no longer trust our natural instincts as mothers, we think we need to buy something to help our children learn and grow and get ahead….

Ladies, let me tell you, the BEST things you can do for your young children are FREE 

You don’t need a fancy toy or gadget, you certainly don’t need an iPad!!! 

The best things you can do to nurture your children and give them a head start is to: 

Talk lots
Play lots
Read aloud lots 
Walk in nature lots
Visit the park lots
Invite curiosity
Teach good manners 

And, through all the above, teach them about Allah 

We are sadly, living in a time where teachers are complaining kids at age 4 and 5 are starting school unable to speak in full sentences, and when given a book try to swipe it!!!! 

Why do you think that is? 

Because as mumas, we’re not engaging with our young children…

We’re not talking to them anymore.

We’re taking them out for dinner at a restaurant and giving them a phone or tablet to watch videos instead of interacting with them at the table 

Honestly ladies, put tablets and phones away. And bring out the books. Bring out the wooden building blocks. Go out for walks together and pick wild flowers. Go for walks together and count the cars or name their colours. 

The best thing you can do to give your children the best head start, is to be with them, engage with them, talk to them, play with them. 

That’s how their vocabulary will grow. 
That’s how they will learn. 
That’s how you both will connect and build a bond. 

Simple things = the BIGGEST impact 🫶

Looking for ways to truly recharge while traveling with your crew? Here’s how you can sneak in moments for yourself—even when you’re juggling a packed family itinerary!

⏰Embrace Early Mornings or Late Nights 
Slip out for a solo sunrise stroll, savour an undisturbed coffee, or unwind alone with a book after everyone’s asleep.

👥Tag-Team With Your Partner or Co-Parent 
Swap kid duties so each adult gets their own break—it could be as simple as a half-hour alone by the pool or a solo errand in town.

🏓Tap Into Kid Clubs, Nannies, or Babysitting Services 
If you are lucky and have a child who enjoys kids clubs, then choose a resort that offers a great variety of activities that are right for the age and personality of your children. Some hotels have spas that offer mini treatments just for kids—everyone gets pampered at the same time! For younger children, look out for hotels with vetted nanny or babysitter services. 

🍦Choose Family-Friendly Dining Spots 
Pick restaurants set on the beach or next to playgrounds. While the kids play within sight, you get a few moments to enjoy your meal and the scenery.

💤Set a “Quiet Hour” for All 
Make it a routine: After lunch, everyone rests, naps, or has solo wind-down time. Devices or audiobooks can keep little ones engaged while you sneak in your own break.

You deserve relaxation too—these small rituals help you return from family adventures feeling refreshed, recharged, and ready for more.

PARENT HACK: Little kid in grown up situations...
Think religious holidays, weddings, dinner out at a fancy restaurant, a 95th birthday celebration. 
It seems like once our little ones surpass the age of 3 (when society says tantrums are no longer acceptable), they are ‘expected’ to be tiny little adults when out in public. And we as parents (me included) feel the pressure for our kids to perform! To say Hello politely, to smile, make conversation, sit nicely at the table, eat with their mouths closed, have calm bodies and keep their indoor voices on! 
Ack!!! It’s too much!

Today this little peanut was thrown into this exact position... and I was kind of nervous walking in, but she nailed it! Ok, ok she may have asked me over 22 times when the cake was coming out, and I may have wanted to pull my hair out because of it but overall, she played the role of ‘mini adult’ like a pro. *** ‘Played the role?’ Yep! Here’s how it worked: leading up to this event we role played what it would be like at an adult party, in a fun and engaging session of imaginary play. It was then that together we discussed appropriate vs. inappropriate behaviours when at a dinner. She LOVED this time with me. We set the table, got dressed up and had some yummy snacks, pretending to be adults! Then today, on our way to our adult party, we reminisced about our recent imaginary party and decided we would ‘do it, just like we did at home!’ Why am I telling you this? In hopes that it helps you!! When children understand what they are walking into and what is expected of them they have an easier time meeting our expectations. 
Tip: Make a secret signal together, a tap on the nose or a secret word like UNICORNS for your child to use when they feel like they just can’t sit still for one more minute. When they use the signal, excuse yourselves from the table and take a quick walk to the bathroom to have a moment of silly together before returning back. It’s ok to take breaks!

Tracking wet diapers is a simple way to ensure your baby is staying hydrated and getting enough to eat! Frequent wet diapers are a great sign that your baby is well-hydrated and healthy. 👶🏻👍🏻

Here’s what to expect:

🍼 Newborns:
• Day 1: At least 1 wet diaper
• Day 2: At least 2 wet diapers
• Day 3: At least 3 wet diapers
• Day 4+: Most newborns will have 6+ wet diapers daily as milk/formula intake increases.

🍼 Infants (1+ week old):
• Expect 6-8 wet diapers daily—a sign of good hydration!

🍼 Older Babies (starting solids):
• Wet diapers may decrease slightly but should still be at least 4-6 per day.

💡 How do you know it’s “wet” enough?
• A wet diaper should feel heavier or contain about 2-4 tablespoons of urine. Many diapers have a wetness indicator strip to help you out!

🚨 When to Be Concerned:
• Fewer than 4 wet diapers per day (after the first week of life)
• Dark or strong-smelling urine
• Baby seems lethargic, has a dry mouth, or cries without tears

If you notice any of these signs, reach out to your pediatrician for guidance! 💕

Parent hack for reducing waste from wet wipes and net reduction of plastic packaging. We can’t claim original credit for this great way of reducing plastics involved in baby wipes but it’s a great #parenthack . You’ll need a roll of paper towel (makes two batches), a plastic container big enough to fit 1/2 roll of paper towel, jab saw, olive oil, organic baby wash, tablespoon measure, kettle to boil water and measuring cup. We normally use #whogivesacrap paper towel but they won’t deliver to our new country house so we’ve been buying the largest number of paper towels in one package from supermarket until we find a workaround. 
1. Cut paper towel in half with jab saw on chopping board.

2. Boil water in kettle.

3. Add 1 tablespoon of olive oil and 1 tablespoon of organic baby wash to measuring jug.

4. Top up to 250ml with boiling water (1 cup for those of you in the United States) and pour over paper towel in your plastic container. Let soak through for 10 minutes and remove cardboard roll. Voila! Cheap eco (low plastic) baby wipes! 
Also better for your kids skin as you’re not using the alcohol in baby wipes on their skin. 
P.S. These baby wipes (just like store bought baby wipes) *can’t be flushed down the toilet* but because they are made completely from paper you could potentially compost them if you have a composting and worm farm setup, hence reducing landfill further.

Parent Hack: Enjoy a candy-free Halloween! 🎃 🍂
Instead of overloading the little one with tons of candy, try these fun alternatives to keep the Halloween spirit alive without the sugar rush.

👻 Halloween-Themed Goodie Bags: Fill bags with non-candy treats like stickers, glow sticks, temporary tattoos, or fun pencils. Kids love collecting these goodies just as much as candy!

🎃 DIY Pumpkin Decorating Kits: Instead of sweets, give out small pumpkins with art supplies (markers, stickers, and paint) for kids to decorate at home. It’s a creative way to celebrate!

🎨 Fall Crafts and Activities: Hand out mini craft kits or activity sheets with Halloween-themed crafts. This keeps kids entertained and encourages creativity.

🍎 Healthy Treats: Consider giving out fun fruit snacks, popcorn balls, or homemade trail mix. You can even make it festive by using Halloween-themed packaging!

🔍 Spooky Scavenger Hunt: Organize a neighborhood scavenger hunt with Halloween-themed items to find instead of candy. Kids will have a blast hunting for treats!
By getting creative with your Halloween treats, you can make the holiday just as special without the candy overload! 🙌

Parent Hack: Enjoy a candy-free Halloween! 🎃 🍂
Instead of overloading the little one with tons of candy, try these fun alternatives to keep the Halloween spirit alive without the sugar rush.

👻 Halloween-Themed Goodie Bags: Fill bags with non-candy treats like stickers, glow sticks, temporary tattoos, or fun pencils. Kids love collecting these goodies just as much as candy!

🎃 DIY Pumpkin Decorating Kits: Instead of sweets, give out small pumpkins with art supplies (markers, stickers, and paint) for kids to decorate at home. It’s a creative way to celebrate!
🎨 Fall Crafts and Activities: Hand out mini craft kits or activity sheets with Halloween-themed crafts. This keeps kids entertained and encourages creativity.

🍎 Healthy Treats: Consider giving out fun fruit snacks, popcorn balls, or homemade trail mix. You can even make it festive by using Halloween-themed packaging!

🔍 Spooky Scavenger Hunt: Organize a neighborhood scavenger hunt with Halloween-themed items to find instead of candy. Kids will have a blast hunting for treats!
By getting creative with your Halloween treats, you can make the holiday just as special without the candy overload! 🙌

👃 Scent helps: Keep it near you for a bit so it picks up a familiar smell - instant reassurance for little ones.

⏰ Make it a cue: Use it at the same points in your routine (nap, bedtime, nursery drop-off). Consistency = quicker settling.

✨ Give busy hands a job: The silky satin edge is perfect for twiddling - great for self-soothing.

🚗 Take it on the go: Pram, car, grandparents - familiar comfort travels well. (Keep straps clear and faces uncovered.)

🔁 Rotate & keep spares: Wash one, use one. If it becomes the favourite, a backup saves the day.

🧼 Care tip: Our double-layer, open-weave bamboo dries fast and stays soft - gentle wash, quick air dry, cuddle again.
